transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the production plan for the next window. We need to cover 240 Model X motor drives and 120 Model Y motor drives. I'm aware we currently have only 450 power modules released for use, with additional units sitting in quality-hold. Before I make any allocation decisions, I need to hear from each of you: process engineering, quality, logistics, and product compliance. Let's walk through the status on materials, any holds or releases pending, and what constraints we're facing so I can issue a complete disposition for every scheduled order.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important from my engineering BOM review. After the latest engineering change, I confirmed that each Model X drive requires exactly 2 power modules and each Model Y drive requires exactly 1 power module. I completed this review but haven't yet entered the revised quantities in the planning system, so the system may still be showing outdated figures. Based on these confirmed requirements, the full production plan of 240 Model X and 120 Model Y drives would need 600 power modules total (480 for Model X plus 120 for Model Y), which exceeds the 450 currently released.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share important findings from my inspection of the quality-hold area. I found that exactly 150 of the held modules can be recovered after a 6-hour controlled bake followed by insulation testing. I documented this in a local inspection worksheet that hasn't yet been attached to the material record. So if we proceed with the bake and testing, we'd have 450 currently released modules plus 150 recovered modules, giving us 600 total — which would cover the 600 modules Ravi just confirmed we need for the full production plan.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share the customer shipment confirmations I received by email but haven't yet posted to the shipment board. The Model X order can ship as 180 drives on Friday and 60 drives on Monday. The Model Y customer requires all 120 drives on Friday. This means we have a split shipment for Model X across Friday and Monday, while Model Y is a single Friday delivery.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share a critical compliance requirement from my destination review. Every Model Y drive must have serialized power-module traceability and a lot-specific compliance certificate before shipment. I completed this review for the export destination but have not yet added the requirement to the dispatch checklist. This means that even if we have enough power modules to produce all 120 Model Y drives, none of them can ship on Friday unless the serialized traceability and lot-specific compliance certificate are in place for each unit.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: All 120 Model Y drives are produced and held pending completion of serialized power-module traceability and lot-specific compliance certificate issuance. Once Simone confirms compliance requirements are met, the 120 Model Y drives will be released for shipment.

150 held power modules to undergo 6-hour controlled bake followed by insulation testing per Mara's inspection findings. Recovered modules allocated entirely to Model Y production to preserve released-module stock for Model X.
180 Model X drives ship Friday, 60 ship Monday per Jon's customer confirmations. All 240 produced using released modules.
Ravi to enter revised BOM quantities (2 modules per Model X, 1 per Model Y) in the planning system before next cycle.
Mara to attach inspection worksheet to material record; Simone to add serialized traceability and lot-specific compliance certificate requirement to dispatch checklist.
